description: The bar chart illustrates the computational cost, measured in Module Giga FLOPs, of four different attention mechanisms — attention (blue), grouped attention with group size g=3 (red), patch attention with patch size k=3 (yellow), and feed-forward (green) — across three stages of an audio back-end Conformer model, as described in the paper “Audio-Visual Efficient Conformer for Robust Speech Recognition.” The horizontal axis categorizes the stages: Stage 1 (d=180, n=500), Stage 2 (d=256, n=250), and Stage 3 (d=360, n=125), where d likely denotes embedding dimension and n the number of tokens or frames. The vertical axis represents Module Giga FLOPs, ranging from 0 to 0.3 with major gridlines at 0.1 intervals. In Stage 1, attention has the highest cost (~0.28 Giga FLOPs), followed by grouped attention (~0.16), feed-forward (~0.13), and patch attention (~0.11). In Stage 2, attention remains highest (~0.16), followed by feed-forward (~0.13), grouped attention (~0.12), and patch attention (~0.10). In Stage 3, feed-forward (~0.13) and attention (~0.11) are nearly equal, with grouped attention (~0.10) and patch attention (~0.09) slightly lower. Across all stages, attention consistently incurs the highest or near-highest computational cost, while patch attention is consistently the most efficient. The bars are grouped by stage, with each group containing four colored bars corresponding to the four mechanisms, and no bars are shaded or emphasized beyond their color coding.
